gen_risks.description: Delays or amendments in passing the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill could prevent establishing the mandatory legal duty on schools to offer free breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor legislative progress closely and ensure policy guidance aligns with statutory developments while encouraging voluntary early uptake.
gen_risks.evidence: the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children to offer a free breakfast club

gen_risks.description: Delays in obtaining timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury could disrupt the April 2026 launch of the Year 1 national rollout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage proactively with HM Treasury through regular business case updates and clear analytical budget projections.
gen_risks.evidence: These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury, effective collaboration with the sector partners

gen_risks.description: Delays in developing the internal CRM system MVP by November 2025 could impair processing school expressions of interest and first-line support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt agile delivery practices for the CRM MVP and establish manual fallback procedures for managing school applications.
gen_risks.evidence: develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: Closure of the National School Breakfast Programme in July 2026 could result in a gap in provision if participating schools are not successfully onboarded by September 2026.
gen_risks.mitigation: Guarantee places for all NSBP schools early, simplify application steps, and coordinate directly with local authority networks.
gen_risks.evidence: ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026.

gen_risks.description: Physical space constraints in primary schools could restrict their ability to accommodate all enrolled pupils for supervised breakfast provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy technical estate advisers to assess facility capacity and help schools implement flexible room management solutions.
gen_risks.evidence: continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints.

gen_risks.description: Administrative burden or perceived financial shortfall could reduce school willingness to engage and join national rollout cohorts prior to statutory mandates.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a simplified funding model with upfront start-up grants and provide direct self-service DfE support materials.
gen_risks.evidence: This should ease the burden and potentially increase willingness to engage and join the programme.

gen_risks.description: Upfront implementation costs combined with delayed attainment benefits could depress short-term value for money and benefit-cost ratio metrics.
gen_risks.mitigation: Track early attendance and readiness metrics while conducting a comprehensive independent evaluation from 2026 to 2028.
gen_risks.evidence: costs are incurred upfront while attainment benefits only materialise after at least one year.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient availability of skilled staff and resources within DfE and the education sector could constrain national rollout delivery capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure delivery support advisers via the education framework and deploy standard guidance toolkits across schools.
gen_risks.evidence: and the availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector.

gen_risks.description: Regional labor market fluctuations exceeding standard area cost adjustments could cause operating budget shortfalls for participating schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct periodic deep-dive funding reviews across cohorts and adjust regional cost formulas in subsequent financial years.
gen_risks.evidence: we apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market.

gen_risks.description: Scaling national rollout to ~2,000 schools based on only one term's worth of learning from the early adopter scheme may introduce unforeseen operational failure modes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an iterative mixed-methods evaluation strategy and phase national rollout across two distinct school cohorts.
gen_risks.evidence: at the point of writing, this business case had one term's worth of learning.

gen_risks.description: Special education needs and disability settings may experience operational deficits if special school funding rates prove inadequate for higher care ratios.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor special school cost structures through process evaluations and provide supplementary targeted local authority support.
gen_risks.evidence: At special schools, the funding rate is: £1,000 start-up grant, daily amount of £18.95, £3.23 for every child

gen_risks.description: Ineffective or delayed data collection mechanisms could compromise monitoring of pupil attendance, participation rates, and compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate a commercial pilot for a call-centre to assist data collection and incorporate administrative tracking features into the internal CRM.
gen_risks.evidence: We will also start commercial processes to begin a call-centre pilot to support data collection.

gen_risks.description: Rising food prices and market inflation could cause school catering expenses to exceed the £1 per child daily variable funding rate.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide national advice on bulk procurement options and track unit catering costs through regular qualitative reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: plus £1 for every child that attends, regardless of characteristics or pupil need.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate coordination or funding delays for local authorities could lead to fragmented regional delivery support for primary schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide direct grant funding to local authorities and establish clear collaborative governance roles.
gen_risks.evidence: we will fund local authorities to support schools and the wider system to effectively deliver free breakfast clubs.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
